title: Understanding the Models
text: Model A includes height in inches and centimeters, and weight in pounds and kilograms. Model B includes only height in centimeters and weight in kilograms. Consider how these variables might affect the confidence intervals.

title: Confidence Intervals and Multicollinearity
text: Think about how multicollinearity might affect the confidence intervals of the parameters in Model A. Multicollinearity occurs when two or more predictors in a model are correlated, potentially inflating the standard errors of the coefficients.

title: Effect of Multicollinearity on Confidence Intervals
text: Multicollinearity can lead to wider confidence intervals, making it more likely for them to include zero. Consider how this might apply to Model A compared to Model B.
